items.title: Wendy Oxenhorn — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I know Bob Cranshaw and Jimmy Owens were finding people who really needed it, because they were all active musicians on the road.

ctx.x: Just his own network. Mostly from Englewood Hospital. The thing is, there wasn’t

really a director at the Jazz Foundation. It was pretty much Herb, Board members... I know Bob Cranshaw and Jimmy Owens were finding people who really needed it, because they were all active musicians on the road. So when they’d hear someone needed it, they would tell Herb, and if it was medical, Herb could let Frank know. They took care of Teri Thornton when she had her cancer. That’s huge. They took care of Rudy Walker when he needed his hip replacement—the amazing saint, Dr. David Feldman. He was and still…
But at the time you assumed the position, had they never had an Executive Director before? Had it been more ad hoc, or...

items.title: Wendy Oxenhorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 22, 2026
items.q: And then some of the guys on our board, Bob Cranshaw and Jimmy Owens, they started reaching out to musicians.

ctx.x: coming back and I introduced him, I asked him to do a gig with this young musician and they got tight. And before we knew it young musicians were asking him to sit in at clubs. So he would guest star. So he was making money. They were getting paid more because they had the famous name and they were becoming like family. So this became a little thing that started happening with some of the elders. So many beautiful things. So okay, Great Night in Harlem. I really didn’t know anything about jazz. In fact I could…

was like this is incredible. “I’m going to give you my top producer.” And he gave us Rick White which was amazing, and Dan Melnick. And then some of the guys on our board, Bob Cranshaw and Jimmy Owens, they started reaching out to musicians. At the time I asked if anyone knew anyone famous. Someone had the number for Bill Cosby’s agent, so I left word. I remember a week later I get a call and I hear this guy with this voice that sounds familiar go, “Wendy?” I was like, “Yes.” He goes, “This is Cos.” Okay. This is…
